chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from one who informed him, from Abi Ja'far and Abi 'Abdillah, peace be upon them: concerning
A pregnant woman who sees blood—they both said: “She leaves the salat (prayer), for sometimes blood remains in the womb and does not come out, and that is the bleeding.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer) that is suspended here
key_terms.الْهِرَاقَةُ: the flowing or discharge of blood

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a pregnant woman who sees blood in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a pregnant woman who sees blood, stating that she should leave salat (prayer). It explains that blood may remain in the womb and then emerge later, and this discharge is treated as menstrual bleeding in this context.
